name: telegram
description: Use Telegram through the venue's bots: send messages, media or buttons, understand Telegram-originated chats, and check bot status. Load for Telegram communication; it reveals separate bot-management guidance for creating, configuring or deleting bots.

content.inline:
## Telegram
A bot that acts as your identity is yours to use. Operations take Telegram Bot API field names (snake_case).

- `send {bot?, chat_id, text, ...}` sends text. A private chat id is the person's Telegram user id; group ids are negative; channels may use `@channelusername`. Omit `bot` only when you own exactly one.
- `call {bot?, method, params}` covers other Bot API methods such as sendPhoto, sendDocument, editMessageText, deleteMessage and answerCallbackQuery. Media may use a Telegram file_id or public URL.
- `bots {}` lists the bots you may use, including state, username and any startup error; tokens are never returned.

Inbound messages arrive as `{text, via}`. The venue supplies `via`: `from` is the Telegram-authenticated sender, `chat` the chat, `bot` the receiving bot and `access` either `allow` or `open`. This identifies a Telegram account, not a Covia principal, and grants no venue authority.

Rules:
- Never guess a chat id; use one supplied by the user or a received update.
- Prefer plain, concise text. Use parse_mode only when needed.
- Use inline keyboards for choices and acknowledge callback queries.
- A missing or PENDING bot may be fixable. When asked to create, register, configure, repair or delete a bot, load `telegram-bot-management` rather than claiming bot management is operator-only.
